compiled_state.title: [test-format-ticket-id-symlink.sh]: assert_equals (undefined) on unreachable setup-failure branches -> 'command not found' instead of diagnostic
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview
Scenario Type: Deferred Review Nitpick (minor, unreachable)

### Expected Behavior
Test diagnostics use a defined assert helper from tests/lib/assert.sh.

### Actual Behavior
tests/scripts/test-format-ticket-id-symlink.sh (added by bug 3203 fix) calls `assert_equals` (NOT defined; only assert_eq/assert_ne/assert_contains/assert_not_contains/assert_pass_if_clean exist) on two setup-failure error branches (~line 119 ticket-creation failure, ~line 133 invalid-symlink). These branches are unreachable on the happy path (the test passes cleanly when fixtures build). If setup ever failed, `assert_equals: command not found` (exit 127 under set -uo pipefail) would print to stderr instead of the intended structured diagnostic. Confirmed by manual dso:code-reviewer-standard@opus during FP-recovery of PR #587 (hash b9a06f61). Fix: replace assert_equals with assert_eq (or the appropriate defined helper) at both call sites.

### Logs/Evidence
PR #587; reviewer hash b9a06f61703f638cd2816d4c5404d6e89894300b659122c191032f8e88a16245

comments.body:
fix-bug:investigation

## VERDICT: LIVE (bug confirmed present at HEAD)

Last commit touching the file: f003467916 (fix(ticket-lib): add -L to find calls in format_ticket_id bash fallback paths)
File: tests/scripts/test-format-ticket-id-symlink.sh

## Confirmed instances of assert_equals (undefined)

Line 67: assert_equals "ticket_created" "" "ERROR: failed to create test ticket"
Line 81: assert_equals "symlink_valid" "invalid" "ERROR: symlink not valid: $symlink_path"

Both are on setup-failure guard branches (unreachable on happy path). assert_equals is NOT defined in tests/lib/assert.sh. Defined helpers are: assert_eq, assert_ne, assert_contains, assert_not_contains, assert_pass_if_clean.

## assert_eq signature

assert_eq(label, expected, actual)

## Correct replacements

Line 67 intent: signal that ticket creation failed (full_id is empty string).
  Current:  assert_equals "ticket_created" "" "ERROR: failed to create test ticket"
  Fix:      assert_ne "ticket_created" "" "$full_id"
  Rationale: The guard is 'if [ -z "$full_id" ]', meaning full_id IS empty. Using
  assert_ne with expected="" and actual="$full_id"=="" would intentionally FAIL
  (recording the failure). But the third arg in the original is a static error string,
  not the actual value — this is diagnostic abuse of the assert API.
  More idiomatic: assert_eq "ticket_created" "created" "" (expected=="created", actual=="" forces FAIL).
  Simplest faithful fix: assert_ne "ticket_created" "" "$full_id"

Line 81 intent: signal that symlink setup is broken.
  Current:  assert_equals "symlink_valid" "invalid" "ERROR: symlink not valid: $symlink_path"
  Fix:      assert_eq "symlink_valid" "valid" "invalid"
  Rationale: The guard is 'if [ ! -L ... ]' meaning symlink IS invalid. We want a
  forced FAIL with a meaningful label. The original third arg is an error string,
  not an 'actual' value. The existing assert_eq on line 164 in Test B shows the
  correct idiom: assert_eq "symlink_valid" "valid" "invalid".

## Sibling assert_equals scan across tests/

Only two instances, both in this single file (lines 67 and 81). No siblings in other files.

## Branches

Both call sites are inside 'if [ -z ... ]' and 'if [ ! -L ... ] || [ ! -d ... ]' guards.
On a healthy test run these branches are never entered; the test passes without
triggering them. If setup fails (e.g. CI git fixture unavailable, tmp filesystem
issue), the branch fires, assert_equals is called, bash exits 127 (command not found)
under set -uo pipefail, and the actual failure reason is swallowed.

## Validation plan

The branches are unreachable on the happy path, so a normal test run cannot exercise them
as a RED test. Options:

Option 1 (RECOMMENDED — proportionate): Direct subshell invocation.
  Simulate the failure branch in a subshell with a forced empty/invalid value:
    (source tests/lib/assert.sh; full_id=""; assert_ne "ticket_created" "" "$full_id")
  This verifies the corrected helper name resolves and produces the intended FAIL output.
  No fixture needed. Runs in <1s.

Option 2 (overkill): Intercept the fixture to force ticket-creation failure.
  Requires mocking the ticket CLI — high complexity for a typo fix.

Recommendation: Option 1 (subshell invocation) is the smallest faithful validation.
The testing classification is GREEN-only (no pre-existing RED state to establish —
the bug is a typo on an unreachable branch, not a logic regression; the RED state
IS the current assert_equals call being undefined, which cannot be practically
automated without a forced-failure fixture). Honest classification: UPDATE
(fixing a static correctness defect on a dead-code branch).

## Feasibility: YES — one-liner replacements, no logic change, no new dependencies.
